questions.text:
When the polynomial 3x⁴ + px³ – 4x + 5 is divided by x – 2, the remainder is 21.

Find the value of p.
questions.markingGuide: By the Remainder Theorem, f(2) = 21. 3(2)⁴ + p(2)³ – 4(2) + 5 = 21. 48 + 8p – 8 + 5 = 21. 8p + 45 = 21. 8p = −24. p = −3. Achieved: Correct value for p.

questions.text:
Solve the equation x² – 6kx = k² for x.
Simplify your answer as far as possible, giving your answer in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: Rearrange: x² – 6kx – k² = 0. Using the quadratic formula: x = (6k ± √(36k² + 4k²))/2 = (6k ± √(40k²))/2 = (6k ± 2k√10)/2 = 3k ± k√10. Achieved: Both solutions for x, in fully simplified form.

questions.text: Prove that the equation (kx)² = 3 – x/k has real roots for all real values of k, where k ≠ 0.
questions.expectedAnswer: The discriminant is 1/(k²) + 12k² > 0 for all real k ≠ 0, so roots are always real.
questions.markingGuide: Rearrange: k²x² + x/k – 3 = 0. Multiply through by k: k³x² + x – 3k = 0. Or keep as k²x² + (1/k)x – 3 = 0. Discriminant = (1/k)² – 4(k²)(−3) = 1/k² + 12k². (1) Since k ≠ 0, 1/k² > 0 and 12k² > 0, so discriminant > 0 for all k. Therefore roots are always real. Achieved: Reaching stage (1) but without justification to explain the required proof. Merit: Clearly justified proof.

questions.text:
Solve the equation z³ + 8m³i = 0, where m is a positive real constant.
Write your solution(s) in polar form, in terms of m.
questions.expectedAnswer: z = 2m cis(–π/6), 2m cis(π/2), 2m cis(7π/6) [or equivalently 2m cis(−5π/6)]
questions.markingGuide: z³ = −8m³i = 8m³ cis(–π/2). r³ = 8m³, so r = 2m. θ = (–π/2 + 2nπ)/3 for n = 0, 1, 2. θ₀ = –π/6, θ₁ = (–π/2 + 2π)/3 = (3π/2)/3 = π/2. Alternatively θ₁ = 7π/6 – wait: θ₁ = (–π/2 + 2π)/3 = (3π/2)/3 = π/2. θ₂ = (–π/2 + 4π)/3 = (7π/2)/3 = 7π/6. So z₁ = 2m cis(–π/6), z₂ = 2m cis(π/2), z₃ = 2m cis(7π/6). Accept equivalent: z₃ = 2m cis(−5π/6). Also accept in cis notation showing cos and sin components. Achieved: One correct solution. Merit: All three correct solutions, with appropriate justification.

questions.text:
The locus of a complex number z is described by |z – 5i| – |z + 5i| = 4.

Find the Cartesian equation of the locus of z, giving your answer in the form ay² – bx² = k, where a, b, k are constants.
questions.markingGuide: Let z = x + yi. |x + (y – 5)i| – |x + (y + 5)i| = 4. √(x² + (y – 5)²) – √(x² + (y + 5)²) = 4. Rearranging and squaring: √(x² + (y – 5)²) = 4 + √(x² + (y + 5)²). (1) Squaring: x² + y² – 10y + 25 = 16 + 8√(x² + (y + 5)²) + x² + y² + 10y + 25. −20y = 16 + 8√(x² + (y + 5)²) + 10y. −30y – 16 = 8√(x² + (y + 5)²). Squaring again: (30y + 16)² = 64(x² + y² + 10y + 25). 900y² + 960y + 256 = 64x² + 64y² + 640y + 1600. 836y² + 320y – 1344 = 64x². Hmm — let me recheck. Alternative: this is a hyperbola with foci at (0,5) and (0,−5), difference of distances = 4, so 2a = 4, a = 2. c = 5. b² = c² – a² = 25 – 4 = 21. Equation: y²/4 – x²/21 = 1, i.e. 21y² – 4x² = 84. (2) E7: Equation of locus found, with clear justification, but with one minor error. E8: Equation of locus found, with clear justification.

questions.text:
The complex numbers u and w are represented on the Argand diagram below.

If z = 2u + 3w, find z, and clearly show it on the Argand diagram above.
questions.markingGuide: From the diagram, u = 4 + 2i (at point (4,2)) and w = −2 – 3i (at point (−2,−3)). z = 2(4 + 2i) + 3(−2 – 3i) = 8 + 4i – 6 – 9i = 2 – 5i. Achieved: Correct value of z found AND plotted on the Argand diagram.

questions.text: If u = m cis(3π/10), write u⁵ in the form a + bi, where a and b are both real numbers, giving your answer in terms of m.
questions.markingGuide: u⁵ = m⁵ cis(5 × 3π/10) = m⁵ cis(3π/2). cis(3π/2) = cos(3π/2) + i sin(3π/2) = 0 + (−1)i = –i. So u⁵ = –m⁵i. Achieved: Correct value of u⁵ found.

questions.text:
Solve the following equation for m, where m is a real number.

|5 – mi| = √(5m²)
questions.markingGuide: |5 – mi| = √(25 + m²). So √(25 + m²) = √(5m²). (1) Squaring: 25 + m² = 5m². 25 = 4m². m² = 25/4. m = ±5/2 = ±2.50. Must have both values. Achieved: Reaching stage (1). Merit: Correct values of m found.

questions.text: If (g + 2i)(3 + hi) = (10 – 4i)(3 – i), then find all possible values of g and h.
questions.expectedAnswer: g = 14/3 and h = −6, or g = 4 and h = −7
questions.markingGuide: RHS: (10 – 4i)(3 – i) = 30 – 10i – 12i + 4i² = 26 – 22i. LHS: (g + 2i)(3 + hi) = (3g – 2h) + (gh + 6)i. Comparing real parts: 3g – 2h = 26. Comparing imaginary parts: gh + 6 = −22, so gh = −28. From 3g – 2h = 26: h = (3g – 26)/2. Substituting: g(3g – 26)/2 = −28. 3g² – 26g + 56 = 0. g = (26 ± 2)/6, giving g = 14/3 or g = 4. When g = 14/3: h = −6. When g = 4: h = −7. Achieved: Establishing the pair of equations for g and h by comparing real and imaginary components. Merit: Finding the two pairs of solutions for g and h.

questions.text: Given that arg((d + 6i)/(1 – di)) = π/4, find the possible value(s) of d, where d is a real constant.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate of denominator: (d + 6i)(1 + di)/((1 – di)(1 + di)) = (−5d + (d² + 6)i)/(1 + d²). (1) Real part = −5d/(1 + d²), imaginary part = (d² + 6)/(1 + d²). If arg = π/4, then Re = Im (both positive): −5d = d² + 6. (2) d² + 5d + 6 = 0. (d + 2)(d + 3) = 0. d = −2 or d = −3. E7: Clear justification to find only one value of d, OR correct solution with one minor error. E8: Clear justification to find both values of d.

questions.text:
One solution of a quadratic equation, with real coefficients, is x = 2 + √pi.

Find the quadratic equation, in terms of p, giving your answer in the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
questions.markingGuide: x = 2 + √(p)i, so the other root is x = 2 – √(p)i (since coefficients are real). Sum of roots = 4. Product of roots = (2 + √p i)(2 – √p i) = 4 + p. So the equation is x² – 4x + (4 + p) = 0. Alternative: [x – (2 + √p i)][x – (2 – √p i)] = (x – 2)² + p = x² – 4x + 4 + p = 0. Achieved: Finding the correct quadratic equation.

questions.text: Expand and simplify (√(3a) – √(12a)i)², giving your answer in terms of a, where a is a real number.

Solve the following equation for x.

(1 + 2√x)(3 + 2√x) = 5 + 6√x
questions.markingGuide: Expand LHS: 3 + 2√x + 6√x + 4x = 3 + 8√x + 4x. Set equal to RHS: 3 + 8√x + 4x = 5 + 6√x. 2√x + 4x = 2. (1) Let u = √x: 4u² + 2u – 2 = 0. 2u² + u – 1 = 0. (2u – 1)(u + 1) = 0. u = 1/2 or u = −1. Since √x ≥ 0, u = 1/2. So √x = 1/2, x = 1/4. But after checking validity, there is only one solution x = 1/4 (x = 1 from u = −1 is eliminated since √x must be non-negative, and checking x = 1: (1+2)(3+2) = 15 ≠ 5 + 6 = 11). Achieved: Reaching stage (1). Merit: Both values of x found, but then x = 1 is eliminated.

questions.text:
One solution of the equation 3z³ + pz² + qz – 8 = 0 is z = 1 + i.

If p and q are both real, find the other two solutions of the equation, and the value of both p and q.
questions.expectedAnswer: p = −10, q = 14; other solutions are z = 1 – i and z = 4/3
questions.markingGuide: Since coefficients are real and z = 1 + i is a solution, z = 1 – i is also a solution. The factor from these two roots is (z – (1+i))(z – (1–i)) = z² – 2z + 2. So f(z) = (3z – 4)(z² – 2z + 2) since leading coefficient is 3 and constant term (−4)(2) = −8. Expanding: 3z³ – 10z² + 14z – 8. Comparing: p = −10, q = 14. The third solution is z = 4/3. Achieved: The other two solutions found, OR either p or q found. Excellence: Both p and q found, with evidence of a fully justified algebraic method.

questions.text:
Given that u and v are both complex numbers, solve the following pair of simultaneous equations, giving solutions in the form a + bi.

ui + 2v = 3
u + (1 – i)v = 4

Show your working clearly.
questions.markingGuide: From equation (2): u = 4 – (1–i)v. Multiplying equation (2) by i: ui + (1–i)iv = 4i, so ui + (i – i²)v = 4i, ui + (i+1)v = 4i. Substituting into equation (1): ui + 2v = 3. From the multiplied eq (2): ui = 4i – (1+i)v. Sub into (1): 4i – (1+i)v + 2v = 3. 4i + v(2 – 1 – i) = 3. 4i + v(1 – i) = 3. v(1–i) = 3 – 4i. v = (3–4i)/(1–i) = (3–4i)(1+i)/((1–i)(1+i)) = (3+3i–4i–4i²)/2 = (3+4–i)/2 = (7–i)/2 = 7/2 – 1/2 i. Then u = 4 – (1–i)(7/2 – 1/2 i) = 4 – (7/2 – 1/2 i – 7i/2 + i²/2) = 4 – (7/2 – 1/2 – 4i) = 4 – 3 + 4i = 1 + 4i. E7: Correct solution but with one minor error. E8: Finding solutions for both u and v.
